newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge probes Bouygues, TF1 chiefs.
newsitem.headline: French judge probes Bouygues, TF1 chiefs.

text.p: The chairmen of French construction giant Bouygues and private television channel TF1 were placed under judicial investigation on Thursday in a probe into alleged kickbacks, justice sources said.
A company spokesman said chairman Martin Bouygues and three other executives placed under investigation would be able to continue their jobs under the terms of their judicial control.

Bouygues, France's biggest construction and public works company, holds the operating licence for TF1, whose chairman is Patrick Le Lay. The other two Bouygues executives were Philippe Chalendon and Bernard Devalan.

Judge Jean-Marie Charpier is investigating some five million francs ($880,000) worth of allegedly false invoices made out by Cerail consultancy firm for subsidiaries of Bouygues including Saur, TF1, Bouygues Offshore and Bouygues Diversifications.

The investigative weekly Le Canard Enchaine said the judge suspected the consultancy firm billed construction companies for ficticious studies as a front for covert payments to conservative political parties.
All France's mainstream political parties are believed to have raised illicit funds through such front companies in the 1980s and early 1990s.

All four executives, placed under investigation on suspicion of misuse of corporate funds, were released after questioning by Charpier on condition that they did not make contact the head of Cerail, Marie-Jacques Dupuybaudy, the justice sources said.
Dupuybaudy, a former vice-president of Bouygues, was placed under investigation last May for allegedly having billed some 40 construction companies for bogus studies from 1986 to 1993.
Martin Bouygues, who is also chairman of Saur, and Chalendon, managing director of the maritime branch of Bouygues Offshore, were held overnight in police custody.
Three other managers of the group have already been placed under investigation by the judge.
